Scaffold `docs/plans/$SLUG.md` (or ask for a slug if `$SLUG` is empty) as a
gate-ready fathom plan. Plans are contract-bearing Markdown checklists, not
prose — this file is self-contained so it works even without fathom's own
source tree present.

## Before writing a single line

1. Confirm `docs/plans/$SLUG.md` doesn't already exist (kebab-case name).
2. Ground every claimed symbol BEFORE it goes in a contract — don't guess
   package paths or symbol names from memory. Call fathom's MCP tools if
   registered (`find_symbol` / `pack_context` to confirm a symbol and its
   real package directory; `test_impact` or `references` to see whether a
   `Test*` already statically reaches it, which tells you up front whether
   `skip_test: true` will be honest or a cover-up).
3. If the plan implements/verifies a spec, get its bracketed ID(s)
   (`[US-042]`, `[EP-013]`, `[FR-7]`, or a milestone form like `M18.2`) —
   `spec_refs` or `traceability` will confirm the ID is real.

## Checklist format

```
- [ ] Title text [SPEC-ID] {id: T-1, symbol: Sym, package: dir/of/sym}
```

- **Checkbox**: `[ ]` open, `[x]` claimed-done (gated), `[~]` in progress
  (never gated), `[-]` skipped (exempt — needs `disposition:`). Never
  hand-write `[x]` for something not actually grounded against the index.
- Keep the title, spec IDs, and the `{…}` annotation ALL on one line — the
  parser is line-based; an annotation on a continuation line is silently
  ignored and the task verifies as `no-contract`.

## Annotation keys (one `{…}` block per gated line)

- `id` — author-owned **stable** task ID (`T-1`, …) — never the positional
  `md-NNN` fallback, which renumbers when lines are inserted above it.
- `symbol` — exact symbol name as it exists in the index.
- `package` — repo-relative directory of the symbol's file; required
  whenever the bare name could exist in more than one package.
- `reachable_from` — an entrypoint the symbol must be statically reachable
  from (optional).
- `min_tier` — minimum evidence tier, default `verified` (loosen explicitly).
- `skip_test: true` — exempts the test-reaches requirement; ALWAYS pair with
  `skip: "<why no test can reach it>"` (non-Go deliverable, generated code,
  a doc/skill file). Never add it just to make a claim pass.
- `allow_contradiction: true` — lets contradictions on the symbol pass.

A `[-]` skipped line needs `disposition: refused|deferred`, a `reason:`
(double-quote any value containing a comma), and for `deferred`, a
`trigger:` — the revival condition, recorded for a future session to grep.

## Before checking any box

```sh
fathom verify --service <svc> --plan docs/plans/$SLUG.md
```

A `fail` means the claim is wrong, not the gate — fix the claim or the code,
never just the checkbox. See the `fathom-verify` prompt/skill for the exit
codes and the fail-open convention.

## Worked skeleton

```markdown
# $SLUG — one-line purpose

- [ ] First unit of work [US-042] {id: T-1, symbol: DoTheThing, package: internal/thing}
- [ ] Second unit, non-Go deliverable {id: T-2, symbol: cmdSomething, package: cmd/yourtool, skip_test: true, skip: "shell-script glue, no Test* can reach it"}
- [-] Nice-to-have, not this wave {id: T-3, disposition: deferred, reason: "needs design review", trigger: "design doc lands"}
```
